name: ICC Profiles
description: ColorProfile, an ICC matrix-and-curve profile as a plain value: RGB (nine colourants, three curves) or gray (its white point, one curve), colourants in XYZ relative to the D50 PCS already Bradford-adapted, curves as gamma, table or parametric (para types 0 to 4 with 1, 3, 4, 5 or 7 parameters); the built-in sRGB (para type 3), Display P3 and linear sRGB profiles have their colourants and parameters rounded to the s15Fixed16 grid, so a written built-in reads back ==. The ICC reader (ICCRead) bounds-checks every offset, size and count with no Int overflow: v2 or v4, display or input class, RGB or GRAY data space and an XYZ PCS; curv tags (0 entries identity, 1 a u8Fixed8 gamma, more a uInt16 table) and para tags; a desc or mluc description; colourants read as stored. Damaged bytes, a missing tag, a LUT-based profile (A2B or B2A tags without the matrix-and-curve tags), CMYK, Lab or another colour space, a Lab PCS, another class or version, and another curve or description type throw ColorError naming the cause. The ICC writer (ICCWrite) emits deterministic v4.3 display bytes (date and profile ID 0): header, tag table, each tag 4-byte aligned and zero-padded, tags with equal bytes shared; mluc desc, then for RGB a D50 wtpt, chad as the Bradford D65-to-D50 matrix, colourants and three TRCs, for gray its white in wtpt and kTRC; wrong value or curve counts, a value outside s15Fixed16 or u8Fixed8, a table under 2 entries or outside 0...1, a para type or count out of range and a size past uInt32 throw ColorError. ProfileTransform maps encoded colours through the D50 PCS: source curves, source colourants, linear Bradford adaptation when the two whites (where RGB 1, 1, 1 or gray 1 lands) differ, inverse target colourants, inverse target curves (tables by binary search, extended past 1); curves are odd-extended and nothing is clamped; a gray source reads the first component and a gray target writes r == g == b. Wrong counts, non-finite values, singular target colourants, a gray white with Y <= 0, a white with a zero cone response, an overflowing matrix and an uninvertible curve (a falling or flat table, gamma <= 0, para slope a <= 0 or linear slope c < 0) throw ColorError.
